claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing banking product and its licensed bank charter crossed via whole-entity statutory merger at the January 1, 2018 effective time, but Section 5.13 shows the data-processing/informational systems that deliver that product had NOT converted at closing — conversion was deferred to "as soon as practicable following the Effective Time," a documented product-vs-process mismatch at closing, contractually absorbed by the Section 5.13 conversion covenant. gap_56=1: the processing substrate and operations were not carried across with the organization/people intact — the founder-CEO was reduced to a single board seat, the COO moved to a regionalized (non-corporate) role, other HCBF officers/directors ceased serving, and a severance schedule contractually priced in anticipated workforce attrition at closing, evidencing process/organization misalignment absorbed via the covered-employee benefits/severance provisions. T1 coded replace because CenterState's own executives and board (plus one HCBF director) governed the surviving company.

gemini.rationale: The customer-facing banking product and legal vehicle crossed at closing via a direct statutory merger (T4), but the underlying operational data-processing systems (T5) had not converted, creating a documented gap_45. This gap was contractually mitigated by Section 5.13 of the merger agreement, which explicitly deferred systems conversion to a post-closing period. No specific structural mismatch between the deferred processes and the transferring organization (T6) was documented at closing, resulting in a 0 for gap_56.

openai.rationale: The customer-facing banking product and licensed bank vehicle crossed at closing through Harbor Community Bank’s merger into CenterState Bank, but the data-processing and electronic systems used to deliver that product were scheduled for conversion only after the effective time, documenting a T4–T5 mismatch at closing [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-327431, DEFM14A, Merger Agreement Section 5.13]. The operational substrate therefore entered a deferred integration process while HCBF’s leadership and organization did not transfer intact: most directors and executive officers ceased serving, the COO moved to a regional role, and employee severance was contractually anticipated [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-327431, DEFM14A]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-000005, Form 8-K (HCBF), Item 5.02]. Section 5.13 contractually bridged the processing mismatch by requiring post-closing systems-integration planning and conversion [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-327431, DEFM14A, Merger Agreement Sections 5.13-5.14].
